title: This Strategy Actually Works Great in Reality Fracture Draft!!!
event: FRA live Arena draft, solo; the Arena pick timer is on and chat is not mentioned; Premier / Quick not named on screen
source: frames read from data/videos/raw/iGzTA_-eFbw (pack title rows and pool counter; layout pool-at-right to P1p6 then pack on top; pick start times from OCR (tesseract) of the Pack|Pick banner; the 40/40 deck screen at 1151 s with the 16-card sideboard row on screen); takes from the transcript, the pool and the deck screen; hover popups hid some cards; transcript from YouTube auto captions, card names corrected; cut-off 1155 s

colour_path.quote: I think Last Gasp is the best of the cards.
it opens me up to just playing like a blue any color deck, and then splashing the green very easily.

picks.reasoning: Fatehold Chronologist over Last Gasp and Keeper: the rare and the pair cards are unplayable; Last Gasp is the best card but he has wanted reps with Chronologist, a middle ground between power and flexibility (hybrid); Keeper is the weakest but colourless.

considered.Keeper of the Quiet Hour: weakest of three, guaranteed to make the cut

quotes: I think Last Gasp is the best of the cards. ... we'll take that one.

picks.reasoning: Fblthp, Impossibly Lost: really good with Chronologist and cheap card draw; he rates Fblthp, Knows the Way (double green) and Hortimancer; Rise of the Deathbringer is good but the minus three, minus three kills few relevant creatures if the format is slow.

considered.Rise of the Deathbringer: pretty good, would be better in a faster format
considered.Fblthp, Knows the Way: really good in any green deck, helps splashing

quotes: Let's just go with this Fblthp. I've been very impressed by it.

picks.reasoning: Mind Meanderer: the best card in the pack, heavy blue and easy to play in blue-green decks, very splashable; the dual land is not helpful; Unsummon is nice.

considered.Stingerquill Charm: far from what he is doing

quotes: I think this is the best card, and it's very splashable.

picks.reasoning: Undulating Witness over the green cards: more flexible, opens a blue-any-colour deck splashing green easily with a landcycler; he notes landcyclers get taken higher and higher and used to wheel at picks eight and nine.

considered.Jiang Yanggu, Never Alone: solid, would put him towards blue-green

quotes: I'd rather take Undulating Witness because it's more flexible.

picks.reasoning: Saheeli, Jewel of Avishkar: wanted to play it for some time, really good with plenty of spells, but eats removal; No Admittance is a very good card, Last Gasp and another Chronologist are in the pack.
quotes: I kind of want to play the Saheeli though, so let's take that.

picks.reasoning: Samut, Hazoret's Champion over Kiora of Salt and Sand and the land: very strong in a tempo deck (random fliers with haste); Kiora is hard to use.
quotes: Samut's very strong when you're building like a more tempo deck.

picks.reasoning: Clash of Elements: 'bang, we're getting all the blue red cards now'; he would second-pick the Annex to help with a Mind Meanderer splash but does not have to try to splash it; Tam's Resistance and Sphinx's Approach are fine in heavy-blue decks.
quotes: This is great, really strong pick up.

picks.reasoning: Traxos, Academy Guardian: really good with the cards he hopes to have in blue-red: play it after an Unsummon and get a three-drop; Gallia is a solid black card.
quotes: Beautiful, we get a Traxos.

picks.reasoning: Artifist Acumen: he does not think it is very good (first strike and a card) but, with no Something Worth Saving in his plan, he tries it; with two Acumens and a Blazing Crescendo it works better.
quotes: Maybe this is the chance to try the acumen, but I just don't think this card's very good.

picks.reasoning: Inspired Tethermage (inferred from the sideboard; no spoken comment): a card he is not otherwise interested in.
Blazing Crescendo: makes random ground creatures hard to block; he jokes of a legendary Chandra's Emberling deck.
quotes: Blazing crescendo does make like your random ground creatures hard to block.

picks.reasoning: Chandra's Emberling: he says it is the sort of thing he will wheel (it wheels from pick 12).
quotes: We will be wheeling the Emberling for sure.

picks.reasoning: Taken card not identified; both cards were hidden.
Last card, never displayed.
Fblthp, Impossibly Lost (second): easy card draw for two mana; he rates Pia highly and would see it later; Lich's Relic is really good but not for this deck.

considered.Pia, Determined Rebuilder: really strong, works well with Saheeli; wheels at pick 9
considered.Lich's Relic: really good, deck does not want it

quotes: I kind of want to take Fblthp, just easy card draw.

picks.reasoning: Mindseeker Oculus over Clash of Elements: he does not want to pass Oculus; better pound for pound; casting it on turn three makes the game great.

considered.Clash of Elements: he would love it, Oculus better

quotes: I kind of just don't ever want to pass Mindseeker Oculus. It's just so strong.

picks.reasoning: Mind Meanderer (second): 'let's just take the Mind Meanderer and just commit to splashing green for him'; his two-drop slot is fine; Chronologist number two is not needed.
quotes: Let's just take the Mind Meanderer and just commit to splashing green for him.

picks.reasoning: Awaken the Inferno over Craftwork Crusher: he does not want the double-green splash and has done that too often; the Crusher is 'insane' but Awaken is a landcycler for a splash that works in a prowess deck; he decides to go blue-red.

considered.Craftwork Crusher: insane, but he does not want the double-green splash

quotes: Let's just not go for the double green splash. I've been doing that a lot.

picks.reasoning: Geist of Saint Thalia (inferred from the deck; Avatar of Burgeoning Echoes, Emberling in the pack): no spoken reason for this pick.
Murmuring Volume over Infinite Coursework: a non-creature spell that helps cast the big cards.
quotes: Murmuring Volume is a non-creature spell that also helps me cast these big guys at the top.

picks.reasoning: Twinned Vision: a cool double-spell card and filtering; Infinite Coursework in the pack.
quotes: Twin Division should be nice.

picks.reasoning: Frostbite Pyromental: 'this is actually the perfect deck for Frostbite Pyromancer. Card draw deals damage; it works well with Fblthp.'
quotes: Card draw deals damage. It works well with Fblthp.

picks.reasoning: Pia, Determined Rebuilder wheeled: he would take the Emberling but Pia is so much better.
quotes: I would take the Chandra's Emberling, but Pia's just so much better.

picks.reasoning: Transformative Commons: a blue-green land to help with the Mind Meanderer splash; the two-drops he wants to be able to play on turn two.
quotes: Let me get a blue green land to help with the Mind Meanderer.

picks.reasoning: Keeper of the Quiet Hour from a weak pack (Yuriko, Mabel, Archive Arbiter).
